displayedInputs.question:
The figure below shows a square and four equilateral triangles, with each triangle having a side lying on a side of the square, such that each triangle has side length \(2\) and the third vertices of the triangles meet at the center of the square. The region inside the square but outside the triangles is shaded. What is the area of the shaded region?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

As shown in the figure, line segment \(\overline{AD}\) is trisected by points \(B\) and \(C\) so that \(AB=BC=CD=2.\) Three semicircles of radius \(1,\) \(\widehat{AEB},\) \(\widehat{BFC},\) and \(\widehat{CGD},\) have their diameters on \(\overline{AD}\), lie in the same halfplane determined by line \(AD\), and are tangent to line \(EG\) at \(E,\) \(F,\) and \(G,\) respectively. A circle of radius \(2\) has its center at \(F.\) The area of the region inside the circle but outside the three semicircles, shaded in the figure, can be expressed in the form \[\frac{a}{b}\cdot\pi-\sqrt{c}+d,\] where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are positive integers and \(a\) and \(b\) are relatively prime. What is \(a+b+c+d?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

The figure below shows line \(\ell\) with a regular, infinite, recurring pattern of squares and line segments.

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

How many of the following four kinds of rigid motion transformations of the plane in which this figure is drawn, other than the identity transformation, will transform this figure into itself?

• some rotation around a point of line \(\ell\)

• some translation in the direction parallel to line \(\ell\)

• the reflection across line \(\ell\)

• some reflection across a line perpendicular to line \(\ell\)

The figure below shows \(13\) circles of radius \(1\) within a larger circle. All the intersections occur at points of tangency. What is the area of the region, shaded in the figure, inside the larger circle but outside all the circles of radius \(1?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

The figure below is a map showing \(12\) cities and \(17\) roads connecting certain pairs of cities. Paula wishes to travel along exactly \(13\) of those roads, starting at city \(A\) and ending at city \(L,\) without traveling along any portion of a road more than once. (Paula is allowed to visit a city more than once.) How many different routes can Paula take?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Right triangle \(ACD\) with right angle at \(C\) is constructed outwards on the hypotenuse \(\overline{AC}\) of isosceles right triangle \(ABC\) with leg length \(1,\) as shown, so that the two triangles have equal perimeters. What is \(\sin(2\angle BAD)?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

As shown in the figure, line segment \(\overline{AD}\) is trisected by points \(B\) and \(C\) so that \(AB=BC=CD=2.\) Three semicircles of radius \(1,\) \(AEB,\) \(BFC,\) and \(CGD,\) have their diameters on \(\overline{AD},\) and are tangent to line \(EG\) at \(E,\) \(F,\) and \(G,\) respectively. A circle of radius \(2\) has its center on \(F.\) The area of the region inside the circle but outside the three semicircles, shaded in the figure, can be expressed in the form

\[ \dfrac{a}{b}\cdot\pi-\sqrt{c}+d, \]

where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are positive integers and \(a\) and \(b\) are relatively prime. What is \(a+b+c+d?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

Three identical rectangles are put together to form rectangle \(ABCD,\) as shown in the figure below. Given that the length of the shorter side of each of the smaller rectangles is \(5\) feet, what is the area in square feet of rectangle \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: The altitude of an equilateral triangle determines half the square's side length. The shaded area is the square's area minus the four triangle areas.
mappings.answerReason: Each triangle has height √(2² - 1²) = √3 and area √3. The square therefore has side 2√3 and area 12, leaving 12 - 4√3.

mappings.rationale: Split the shaded region at AD and EG into an upper semicircle, gaps within a rectangle, and a lower circular segment. The segment is evaluated as a sector minus a triangle.
mappings.answerReason: The upper part has area 2π, and the middle gaps have area 4 - π. Since AD is distance 1 from F, the lower segment has central angle 120° and area 4π/3 - √3. The total is 7π/3 - √3 + 4, so (a,b,c,d) = (7,3,3,4), whose sum is 17.

mappings.rationale: The task asks whether the infinite pattern has half-turn, translation, and reflection symmetries. The diagonal attachments distinguish the reflection cases.
mappings.answerReason: A half-turn about a suitable point on ℓ preserves the pattern, as does translation by two square widths. Reflection across ℓ or any perpendicular line reverses the slant of the diagonal attachments, so neither preserves it. Exactly two kinds work.

mappings.rationale: Tangency makes adjacent unit-circle centers distance 2 apart. The staggered rows determine the enclosing radius, after which the thirteen unit-disk areas are subtracted.
mappings.answerReason: The vertical separation of adjacent staggered rows is √(2² - 1²) = √3. The top circle's center is therefore 2√3 from the enclosing circle's center, giving radius R = 1 + 2√3. The shaded area is πR² - 13π = 4π√3.

mappings.rationale: An allowed route is a trail with thirteen distinct edges. Vertex-degree parity constrains the four omitted roads, and independent choices of cycle direction determine the route count.
mappings.answerReason: The omitted edges must have odd degree at the six odd-degree grid vertices and at A and L. Four edges supply exactly these eight endpoints, uniquely forcing the omissions. The remaining graph has two four-edge cycles joined by a bridge, with a tail to each endpoint. Each cycle can be traversed in either direction, giving 2 × 2 = 4 routes.

mappings.rationale: Equal perimeters give CD + AD = 2, and Pythagoras determines these lengths. One route uses ∠BAD = 45° + ∠CAD. Alternatively, coordinates give the positive horizontal and vertical projection lengths of AD, allowing evaluation of sin(2∠BAD) as twice their product divided by AD².
mappings.answerReason: Write CD = x and AD = y. Then x + y = 2 and y² - x² = AC² = 2, so y - x = 1, giving x = 1/2 and y = 3/2. For θ = ∠CAD, sin θ = 1/3. Thus sin(2∠BAD) = sin(90° + 2θ) = cos 2θ = 1 - 2/9 = 7/9.

mappings.rationale: Split the shaded region at AD and EG into an upper semicircle, gaps within a rectangle, and a lower circular segment. The segment is evaluated as a sector minus a triangle.
mappings.answerReason: The upper part has area 2π, and the middle gaps have area 4 - π. Since AD is distance 1 from F, the lower segment has central angle 120° and area 4π/3 - √3. The total is 7π/3 - √3 + 4, so (a,b,c,d) = (7,3,3,4), whose sum is 17.

mappings.rationale: The rotated identical rectangle on the right shows that each smaller rectangle's longer side equals two shorter sides. These dimensions determine the larger rectangle's area.
mappings.answerReason: The longer side of each small rectangle is 2 × 5 = 10 feet. The large rectangle consequently measures 10 by 10 + 5 = 15 feet, so its area is 150 square feet.
